correctness.rationale: Writing h=g/a and Q(u)=u+h(1-F)tanh(u), the implicit sample equation is Q(u)=Fx. Q is a strictly increasing bijection, including at theta=0 and theta=1. The sample-coordinate map is Q(u_next)=Eu-h(F-E)tanh(u). The mesh derivative at x corresponding to u is m(q)=[E-h(F-E)q]/[1+h(1-F)q] with q=sech^2(u). It ranges from m(1) to E, with 1+m(1)=(1+E-h*Delta)/(1+h(1-F)); this proves the sharp exponential regimes. Interpolation has a bounded multiplier on each unit interval. At equality |P(x)|<|x| for x nonzero although the uniform derivative bound is one. Expanding Q and its inverse yields P(x)=-x+Kx^3+O(x^5), and differences of |x_k|^{-2} tend to 2K on non-finite-hitting orbits. Above threshold m(1)<-1; the equation P(c)=-c forces u=Cc and has exactly one positive solution since tanh(z)/z strictly decreases. Its derivative satisfies m(sech^2(Cc))>m(h_c/h)=-1, and is less than E; the cycle multiplier is the square of this derivative. Odd interpolation gives anti-periodicity. P(x)<x for x>0, so no nonzero fixed point, and the amplitude expansion follows from tanh(z)/z=1-z^2/3+O(z^4). An independent sample-coordinate numerical check at E=1/2, F=7/8, h_c=6 gave K=1/14 and k*x_k^2/7=0.999364 at k=100000; at h=6.3 it gave c=0.778482 and a two-step multiplier about 0.83864. These are corroboration, not the proof; the frozen script was not run.
residual_risks: Exponential attraction at criticality fails even locally as a uniform estimate and non-finite-hitting orbits have the algebraic rate. Supercritical stability and uniqueness are only for the specified symmetric orbit, not a basin or attractor classification.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Right-endpoint sampling is the elementary implicit step u+h(1-E)tanh(u)=Ex with P(x)=u, so |P(x)|<=E|x|. Anti-periodic interpolation follows by oddness, the relative O(g-g_c) term by the next Taylor order of the identical amplitude equation, and no nonzero time-one orbit by the sign of feedback. No substantial noncovered remainder survives.
